title: Joshua 20:4–6 (the elders' hearing at the gate) — absent from Brenton’s Greek
summary: Joshua 20:4–6 in the KJV describes a hearing at a refuge city's gate. It also describes the stay until the high priest dies. The Hebrew text includes these verses. The cited page of the old Greek translation jumps from verse 3 to verse 7.
text: KJV Joshua 20:4–6: “And when he that doth flee unto one of those cities shall stand at the entering of the gate of the city, and shall declare his cause in the ears of the elders of that city, they shall take him into the city unto them, and give him a place, that he may dwell among them. And if the avenger of blood pursue after him, then they shall not deliver the slayer up into his hand; because he smote his neighbour unwittingly, and hated him not beforetime. And he shall dwell in that city, until he stand before the congregation for judgment, and until the death of the high priest that shall be in those days: then shall the slayer return, and come unto his own city, and unto his own house, unto the city from whence he fled.” Hebrew text Joshua 20:4–6: וְנָ֞ס אֶל־אַחַ֣ת ׀ מֵהֶעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְעָמַד֙ פֶּ֚תַח שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֔יר וְדִבֶּ֛ר בְּאָזְנֵ֛י זִקְנֵ֥י הָעִֽיר־הַהִ֖יא אֶת־דְּבָרָ֑יו וְאָסְפ֨וּ אֹתֹ֤ו הָעִ֙ירָה֙ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְנָתְנוּ־לֹ֥ו מָקֹ֖ום וְיָשַׁ֥ב עִמָּֽם׃ וְכִ֨י יִרְדֹּ֜ף גֹּאֵ֤ל הַדָּם֙ אַֽחֲרָ֔יו וְלֹֽא־יַסְגִּ֥רוּ אֶת־הָרֹצֵ֖חַ בְּיָדֹ֑ו כִּ֤י בִבְלִי־דַ֙עַת֙ הִכָּ֣ה אֶת־רֵעֵ֔הוּ וְלֹֽא־שֹׂנֵ֥א ה֛וּא לֹ֖ו מִתְּמֹ֥ול שִׁלְשֹֽׁום׃ וְיָשַׁ֣ב ׀ בָּעִ֣יר הַהִ֗יא עַד־עָמְדֹ֞ו לִפְנֵ֤י הָֽעֵדָה֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט עַד־מֹות֙ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּדֹ֔ול אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִהְיֶ֖ה בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֑ם אָ֣ז ׀ יָשׁ֣וּב הָרֹוצֵ֗חַ וּבָ֤א אֶל־עִירֹו֙ וְאֶל־בֵּיתֹ֔ו אֶל־הָעִ֖יר אֲשֶׁר־נָ֥ס מִשָּֽׁם׃ [… 20:4–6 as in the KJV: the slayer states his case to the elders at the gate, is not handed to the avenger, and stays until trial and the death of the high priest.] Old Greek translation Joshua 20:3 and 20:7, the verses either side of the gap: Φυγαδευτήριον τῷ φονευτῇ τῷ πατάξαντι ψυχὴν ἀκουσίως· καὶ ἔσονται ὑμῖν αἱ πόλεις φυγαδευτήριον, καὶ οὐκ ἀποθανεῖται ὁ φονευτὴς ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀγχιστεύοντος τὸ αἷμα, ἕως ἂν καταστῇ· ἐναντίον τῆς συναγωγῆς εἰς κρίσιν. Καὶ διέστειλε τὴν Κάδης ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Νεφθαλὶ, καὶ Συχὲμ ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Ἐφραὶμ, καὶ τὴν πόλιν Ἀρβὸκ, αὕτη ἐστὶ Χεβρὼν, ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Ἰούδα. [… the Greek page runs from verse 3 straight to verse 7: no gate, no elders, no mention of the high priest’s death in the Greek of this chapter. Verse 3 and verse 9 do end with “until he stand before the congregation for judgment”.] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JOS20.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/6/20/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JOS20.htm.
reasoning: The KJV and Hebrew text include three verses of procedure that this Greek page does not print. Greek verses 3 and 9 still describe refuge until the person stands before the community.
scope: The finding covers Joshua 20:4, 20:5 and 20:6 only. It does not establish whether Greek lost the verses or Hebrew gained them. title: Ephraim “went northward” (Judges 12:1) — the Greek has a place, “Boraran”
summary: KJV Judges 12:1 says the men of Ephraim “went northward”. The Hebrew word is צָפֹונָה (tsaphonah); the Greek prints the place name Βοῤῥᾶν instead of a direction.
text: KJV Judges 12:1: “And the men of Ephraim gathered themselves together, and went northward, and said unto Jephthah, Wherefore passedst thou over to fight against the children of Ammon, and didst not call us to go with thee? we will burn thine house upon thee with fire.” Hebrew (WLC) Judges 12:1: וַיִּצָּעֵק֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶפְרַ֔יִם וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ר צָפֹ֑ונָה וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ לְיִפְתָּ֜ח מַדּ֣וּעַ ׀ עָבַ֣רְתָּ ׀ לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם בִּבְנֵי־עַמֹּ֗ון וְלָ֙נוּ֙ לֹ֤א קָרָ֙אתָ֙ לָלֶ֣כֶת עִמָּ֔ךְ בֵּיתְךָ֕ נִשְׂרֹ֥ף עָלֶ֖יךָ בָּאֵֽשׁ׃ [… and the man of Ephraim was summoned and crossed to/toward the north (or: to Zaphon) and they said to Jephthah …] Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Judges 12:1: Καὶ ἐβόησεν ἀνὴρ Ἐφραὶμ, καὶ παρῆλθαν εἰς Βοῤῥᾶν, καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς Ἰεφθάε, διατί παρῆλθες παρατάξασθαι ἐν υἱοῖς Ἀμμὼν, καὶ ἡμᾶς οὐ κέκληκας πορευθῆναι μετὰ σοῦ; τὸν οἶκόν σου ἐμπρήσομεν ἐπὶ σὲ ἐν πυρί. [… and a man of Ephraim cried out, and they passed over to Borran, and they said to Jephthah …] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JDG12.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/7/12/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JDG12.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew word can be read as a direction (“to the north”) or as the place Zaphon. The KJV takes the direction; the Greek has a name.
scope: T applies at Judges 12:1 only. The difference is direction against place name in this one word. The Hebrew form can carry either sense, so this record does not say the KJV mistranslates or that the Greek name is a different site from Zaphon. It does not identify Boraran. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. title: Jephthah “buried in one of the cities of Gilead” (Judges 12:7) — the Greek has “in his city Galaad”
summary: The KJV puts Jephthah's burial “in one of the cities of Gilead”. The Hebrew text uses cities of Gilead. The old Greek translation instead has his city, Galaad.
text: KJV Judges 12:7: “And Jephthah judged Israel six years. Then died Jephthah the Gileadite, and was buried in one of the cities of Gilead.” Hebrew text Judges 12:7: וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֥ט יִפְתָּ֛ח אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שֵׁ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֑ים וַיָּ֗מָת יִפְתָּח֙ הַגִּלְעָדִ֔י וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּעָרֵ֥י גִלְעָֽד׃ פ [… and Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in the cities of Gilead (plural).] Old Greek translation Judges 12:7: Καὶ ἔκρινεν Ἰεφθάε τὸν Ἰσραὴλ ἓξ ἔτη· καὶ ἀπέθανεν Ἰεφθάε ὁ Γαλααδίτης, καὶ ἐτάφη ἐν πόλει αὐτοῦ Γαλαάδ. [… and Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in his city Galaad (singular, with “his”).] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JDG12.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/7/12/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JDG12.htm.

title: Micah pays the Levite “by the year” (Judges 17:10) — the Greek has “a day”
summary: Judges 17:10 in the KJV offers the Levite ten shekels of silver “by the year”. The old Greek translation gives ten of silver for a day. The Hebrew text uses a phrase involving days.
text: KJV Judges 17:10: “And Micah said unto him, Dwell with me, and be unto me a father and a priest, and I will give thee ten shekels of silver by the year, and a suit of apparel, and thy victuals. So the Levite went in.” Hebrew text Judges 17:10: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ לֹ֨ו מִיכָ֜ה שְׁבָ֣ה עִמָּדִ֗י וֶֽהְיֵה־לִי֮ לְאָ֣ב וּלְכֹהֵן֒ וְאָנֹכִ֨י אֶֽתֶּן־לְךָ֜ עֲשֶׂ֤רֶת כֶּ֙סֶף֙ לַיָּמִ֔ים וְעֵ֥רֶךְ בְּגָדִ֖ים וּמִחְיָתֶ֑ךָ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ הַלֵּוִֽי׃ [… ten (of) silver for the days, and an order of garments, and your keep.] Old Greek translation Judges 17:10: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Μιχαίας, κάθου μετʼ ἐμοῦ, καὶ γίνου μοι εἰς πατέρα καὶ εἰς ἱερέα, καὶ ἐγὼ δώσω σοι δέκα ἀργυρίου εἰς ἡμέραν, καὶ στολὴν ἱματίων, καὶ τὰ πρὸς ζωήν σου. [… ten (of) silver for a day, and a robe of garments, and what is for your living.] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/JDG17.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/7/17/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JDG17.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew days phrase can express a year's span, as the KJV renders it. The Greek gives a daily interval, producing a different pay period.
scope: The finding concerns only the year/day contrast at Judges 17:10. The unstated silver unit in Hebrew and Greek is not another finding. The record does not decide the intended interval, establish an exact wage or claim the Greek misread its source. text: KJV Judges 17:5: “And the man Micah had an house of gods, and made an ephod, and teraphim, and consecrated one of his sons, who became his priest.” Hebrew text Judges 17:5: וְהָאִ֣ישׁ מִיכָ֔ה לֹ֖ו בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אֵפֹוד֙ וּתְרָפִ֔ים וַיְמַלֵּ֗א אֶת־יַ֤ד אַחַד֙ מִבָּנָ֔יו וַיְהִי־לֹ֖ו לְכֹהֵֽן׃ [… Micah had a house of ’elohim; and he made an ephod and teraphim …] Old Greek translation Judges 17:5: Καὶ ὁ οἶκος Μιχαία αὐτῷ οἶκος Θεοῦ· καὶ ἐποίησεν ἐφὼδ καὶ θαραφίν· καὶ ἐπλήρωσε τὴν χεῖρα ἀπὸ ἑνὸς υἱῶν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτῷ εἰς ἱερέα. title: Orpah “kissed her mother in law” (Ruth 1:14) — the Greek adds that she returned to her people
summary: KJV Ruth 1:14 says Orpah kissed her mother-in-law but Ruth clave to her. Brenton’s Greek adds καὶ ἐπέστρεψεν εἰς τὸν λαὸν αὐτῆς, “and she returned to her people”, which the Hebrew of this verse does not have.
text: KJV Ruth 1:14: “And they lifted up their voice, and wept again: and Orpah kissed her mother in law; but Ruth clave unto her.” Hebrew (WLC) Ruth 1:14: וַתִּשֶּׂ֣נָה קֹולָ֔ן וַתִּבְכֶּ֖ינָה עֹ֑וד וַתִּשַּׁ֤ק עָרְפָּה֙ לַחֲמֹותָ֔הּ וְר֖וּת דָּ֥בְקָה בָּֽהּ׃ [… and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, and Ruth clung to her.] Septuagint (Brenton Greek) Ruth 1:14: Καὶ ἐπῇραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν, καὶ ἔκλαυσαν ἔτι· καὶ κατεφίλησεν Ὀρφὰ τὴν πενθερὰν αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐπέστρεψεν εἰς τὸν λαὸν αὐτῆς· Ῥοὺθ δὲ ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῇ. [… and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, and returned to her people; but Ruth followed her.] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/RUT01.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/8/1/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/RUT01.htm.
reasoning: In the Hebrew the departure of Orpah is implied until Naomi says in verse 15 that she “is gone back”. The Greek states it in verse 14 as well.

title: “The Almighty hath dealt very bitterly” (Ruth 1:20) — the Greek has “the Sufficient One”

title: “The LORD hath testified against me” (Ruth 1:21) — the Greek has “the Lord humbled me”
summary: At Ruth 1:21, the KJV has Naomi say “the Lord hath testified against me”. The old Greek translation says the Lord humbled her.
text: KJV Ruth 1:21: “I went out full and the Lord hath brought me home again empty: why then call ye me Naomi, seeing the Lord hath testified against me, and the Almighty hath afflicted me?” Hebrew text Ruth 1:21: אֲנִי֙ מְלֵאָ֣ה הָלַ֔כְתִּי וְרֵיקָ֖ם הֱשִׁיבַ֣נִי יְהוָ֑ה לָ֣מָּה תִקְרֶ֤אנָה לִי֙ נָעֳמִ֔י וַֽיהוָה֙ עָ֣נָה בִ֔י וְשַׁדַּ֖י הֵ֥רַֽע לִֽי׃ [… and the Lord has ‘anah in me (answered/testified against me, or afflicted me) …] Old Greek translation Ruth 1:21: Ἐγὼ πλήρης ἐπορεύθην, καὶ κενὴν ἀπέστρεψέ με ὁ Κύριος· καὶ ἱνατί καλεῖτέ με Νωεμὶν, καὶ Κύριος ἐταπείνωσέ με, καὶ ὁ ἱκανὸς ἐκάκωσέ με; [… and the Lord has humbled me, and the Sufficient One has treated me ill.] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/RUT01.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/8/1/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/RUT01.htm.
reasoning: Testifying against someone suggests a courtroom scene; humbling someone does not carry that same image. Naomi's next clause also describes harm. These printed renderings differ without establishing which Hebrew sense is correct.
